# T9 — Bounded replication in five other RTFP countries (Task 6.1)

*Generated by `analysis/t9_replication.py note` from `outputs/tables/T9_*.csv`; do not edit numbers by hand. Exploratory: the selection rule is in `docs/analysis_plan.md` §5, which is a draft not yet posted on OSF.*

**Claim.** On 5 other RTFP countries (42 country-items), with the Bangladesh pipeline and three disclosed changes (markets whose name moves > 3 km across releases are dropped and listed; the noise sample is all markets over six years because the Division filter does not transfer; the WFP audit series is chosen from the data), results **vary across countries and items rather than replicate uniformly**:
- Cross-sectional both-imputed local correlation: median 0.206 (range -0.641 to 0.690) across the 32 items where it is defined (33 items have ≥ 10 pairs; it is undefined when all survey changes are identical). It is positive for 29 of 32, but its 95% interval excludes zero for only 5 (4 positive: MMR salt, COD oil, MLI maize_fao, MLI millet_fao; 1 negative: COD cassava).
- Noise-corrected ρ*: in [0.5, 1] for 7 of 32 items; 3 more exceed 1 and are not interpretable as correlations (small update-only subsets with low estimated reliability). With variant A alone: in [0.5, 1] for 5 of 32 (1 exceed 1).
- Forecast stratum: median 0.037 (range -0.077 to 0.421) (38 items); no interval excludes zero (0 of 38); ρ* in [0.5, 1] for 0 of 38 (2 exceed 1).
- Items whose plain column passed the ≥ 90% audit (35): cross-sectional correlation median 0.185 (range -0.641 to 0.690) (27 items); ρ* in [0.5, 1] for 6 of 27 (1 exceed 1).
- Persistent survey spikes caught by a same-direction published move: 1842 of 6435 (28.6%).
- Level-error outliers from scale mismatches: 14 items have clean cells whose published value is > 5× or < 0.2× the survey value (a unit or scale error, not imputation error); see `T9d_scale_mismatch.csv` for MAPE without them.

## 1. Country selection (fixed before any country's results)

- Rule (analysis plan §5): >= 50 market-file vintages; >= 30 markets in latest vintage (excl. 'Market Average'); plain survey columns present (header and >= 1 value); not Bangladesh; top 5 by markets, ties by vintages, then ISO3.
- Applied at **2026-10-09T08:01:57+00:00** to 39 per-country RTFP market datasets other than Bangladesh (union of the all-country metadata `WLD_2021_RTFP_v02_M`, "37 countries, 3181 markets, 2007/01/01-2026/10/01, version 2026/10/05", and the catalogue search). 25 were eligible. The selection file was written by the `select` stage before the `download` and `run` stages existed for these countries; the run stage refuses to start without it and reuses its listing snapshot (vintages up to the latest seen at selection).
- "Plain survey columns present" was read as a plain item column with at least one value; the selection is identical under the header-only reading.

- Every country was processed **item by item** (one stacked panel per item, via `rtfp.vintages.build_stack(dir, items=[item], prefix=ISO3)`) to bound memory on a 16 GB machine; the largest per-item process peak is in the table.
- Vintages lacking an item are skipped for that item (as for Bangladesh rice). Items = those with both a plain and a `c_` column in the latest vintage.
- Older releases (to January 2024) name the month column `DATES` instead of `price_date`. The extracted working copy renames the header only; data bytes are unchanged. Check over all 99 such vintages: every `DATES` value is the first of the month given by `year`/`month` (0 inconsistent).
- Market identity guard (`rtfp.crosswalk.build_crosswalk`: a name may not move > 3 km or map to two ids in one release): see the table.

## 3. Results by country and item

Clean strata only (fc = forecast, cs = cross-sectional). Levels pool both clean strata (c_final vs the latest-vintage survey value). Local changes: own-release μ, both-imputed pairs, corr not estimated below 10 pairs. ρ* cons. = largest credible of corr/√rel over noise variants A (all pairs) and B (non-zero truth changes), naive and AR(1) estimators, as Gate G1. rel A = naive reliability, variant A. CIs: two-way (market × month) pigeonhole bootstrap, B = 500; reliability held fixed.

## 4. Raw-column audit (Task 1.2 transferred)

Every selected country has a WFP/HDX feed (`hdx_package` in `T9_replication.csv`), so the plain-column assumption was tested for every item: observed cells of the latest vintage are matched to Retail rows of the feed (market by exact name, else nearest within 5 km; same month) with `rtfp.audit.audit_cells`. RTFP item names do not name a WFP commodity variety, so for each item the Retail commodity × unit series with the most exact matches (|y/p − 1| ≤ 1%) was chosen from the data; choosing the best of several candidates can only raise the match share (runner-up shown in `T9c_audit.csv`). Bangladesh's stop-gate was 90%.

## 5. Method facts

- Pipeline: `src/rtfp/replicate.py` (driver; tests in `tests/test_replicate.py` on synthetic inputs) calling `rtfp.vintages` (stack, hold-out, strata toggle > unconfirmed > backfill (> 6 months) > forecast > cross-sectional, change pairs), `rtfp.noise`, `rtfp.metrics` and `rtfp.audit`; the only change from Bangladesh is `build_stack(..., on_drift='drop')`, which removes markets whose name moves > 3 km across releases (geocoding defects) and records them per item in `dropped_markets_location_jump`.
- Noise variant A for every country: all markets except 'Market Average', price months from 6 years before the latest vintage month; variant B drops exact-zero changes. There is no Division-series equivalent outside Bangladesh, so Table 1's A_main filter is not transferable.
- Bootstrap clusters as Tables 2–3: hold-out markets × months for levels, latest-panel markets × months for correlations; seed 20261012.
- Downloads: 509 market-file vintages for the five countries plus the latest file of every candidate, `data/raw/rtfp_other/` with sha256 manifest `data/raw/rtfp_other/MANIFEST.csv`; ≥ 1.2 s between requests. Results computed 2026-10-09T14:22:54+00:00.

## 6. Caveats

- Exploratory. The selection rule was written before these countries' results were computed, but the analysis plan is not yet registered; the results are not confirmatory.
- The commodity series used in the audit is chosen from the data (upward-biased match share); the variety behind each RTFP item is not documented in the files.
- Items whose names end in `_fao` presumably come from a non-WFP (FAO) source; this is an inference from the name only.
- ρ* intervals are not reported: the reliability is held fixed in the bootstrap (Table 1c resamples it jointly for Bangladesh). Holm correction is not applied; no hypothesis is tested here.
- Clean-strata sample sizes differ widely between items; correlations with few pairs have wide intervals (see CIs).
- Fig 9 (forest plot of ρ* bands) is not produced by this script; its inputs are the `corr_*`, `rho_star_*` and `rel_*` columns of `T9_replication.csv`.

**Files.** `outputs/tables/T9_country_selection.csv`, `T9_replication.csv` (country × item, all metrics), `T9b_noise.csv` (reliability by variant), `T9c_audit.csv` (raw-column audit); downloads in `data/raw/rtfp_other/`.
